notes:
Summary: Enterprise logistics platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for latency-sensitive chat and reranking. Prefers VPC deployment with optional on‑prem connectors for regulatory lanes. Wants binding throughput guarantees and a clear reserved GPU sizing plan.

Customer context: Alderbridge operates a global freight marketplace (2000+ employees, heavy NA + EU volume). Live traffic: intermittent peaks driven by booking windows. Currently prototypes with in-house CPU inference and 3rd-party hosted APIs — cost and latency unpredictable.

Technical requirements (from discovery call):
- Primary workloads: chat-support (session state, embeddings lookups), realtime reranking on search results, nightly bulk-embedding pipeline.
- Steady-state target: ~30 QPS average during business hours, ~80k tokens/sec sustained across models (all routes combined).
- Peak/burst target: up to 250 QPS for short windows (10-15 minutes) with spiky tail events at end of booking windows.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for chat-turns (single-turn 0–200 tokens), p99 <= 600ms; reranking p95 <= 300ms.
- Availability: 99.95% SLA for dedicated pools; automatic fallback to cheaper model variants on regional capacity pressure.
- Model preferences: prefer GGML-compatible quantized Llama variants for cost, but want Redwood-verified 70B / 13B families plus an option to run our proprietary 30B model.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high; committed reserved pricing acceptable if burst/overflow economics clear.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration for key management, audit logging for generation events, and EU data residency for EU customer traffic.

POC & workshop timeline:
- 2026-01-15: Intro + product demo (Fireflies ff_20260115_1845) — they provided sample logs and a 2-week test dataset.
- 2026-02-05: Security questionnaire returned (partial) — need clarifications on key rotation and HSM usage.
- 2026-02-20: Throughput baseline call (Fireflies ff_20260220_0932) — ran synthetic replay, observed 18 QPS on in-house; Redwood suggested batching + prefix KV cache.
- 2026-03-01: Pricing/ROI draft sent (drive://rdw/pricing/alderbridge-dedicated-deck-2026-03.pdf).
- 2026-03-18: On-site sizing workshop scheduled (Nora + Diego + infra eng lead + security). Goal: finalize reserved GPU count, autoscale policy, and SLA terms.

Preliminary capacity plan (workshop deliverable expectations):
- Steady-state: plan to reserve 4 H100-like nodes (or equivalent multi-GPU pool) sized to sustain 30 QPS with 75ms median token latency for the preferred 13B variant.
- Burst capacity: policy to allow automatic burst to 12 nodes with pre-warmed model kernels for 10–20min windows; billing/commitment model to include burst credits.
- Token/sec assumption: average 80 tokens/request -> steady tokens/sec ~2400 (30 QPS) and peak tokens/sec ~20k (250 QPS). Workshop to validate with replayed traces.
- Batching & caching levers: enable continuous batching for reranking paths; prefix KV cache for repeated conversational context (expected 20–30% token savings).
- Fallback policy: route to smaller quantized variant (13B q4) or hosted capacity in another region when dedicated pool saturated; need contractual latency cap for fallback flows.

SLA negotiation points to prepare:
- Availability target: 99.95% for reserved pools, credits for repeat p99 latency misses.
- Throughput guarantee: committed baseline QPS for provisioned nodes, with explicit headroom % for autoscale ramp.
- Incident response: enterprise SRE escalation, 2‑hour P1 response, postmortem cadence.
- Data handling: log retention window, access controls, and ability to exclude EU traffic from US compute.

Open items / asks from Alderbridge:
- Request: detailed per-GPU perf numbers for their preferred model family (13B & 30B) in 8-bit vs 4-bit paths.
- Request: concrete cost model showing reserved + burst vs fully-hosted run for 12-month window.
- Ask: sample SLA language for throughput guarantees and fallback economics.
- Need: network diagram for VPC peering and expected egress patterns to complete security review.

Sales cues & internal notes:
- Competitive risk: they are running a parallel RFQ including CloudAI Endpoints and internal scaling program. Price sensitivity high for long-tail cost.
- Strategy: emphasize Redwood's unified runtime (same config for dedicated/private), show Optimize recommendations that reduce token/sec by intelligent caching.
- Demo ops: bring a short live replay of peak 2025-11-17 traffic to the on-site workshop to validate autoscale timing.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver perf matrices (Diego) by 2026-03-12.
- Legal & security draft to be handed to Alderbridge legal on 2026-03-16.
- Run replay test during on-site workshop and produce finalized reserved GPU recommendation within 7 business days after workshop.
